content.title: What projected Super El Niño could mean for the Carolinas
content.text: GREENVILLE, S.C. (FOX Carolina) - El Niño is projected to develop during summer of 2026, and it could become a ‘super’ El Niño. NOAA shared in a recent update that the chance of El Niño development has risen to 62% during the months of June, July and August. The forecast for a super El Niño is a 1-in-3 chance by October, November and December of 2026. A super El Niño can be defined as water temperatures being above average over several months by at least 1.5°C.It can have impacts on the weather in the U.S., which could potentially lead to impacts here in the Carolinas. El Niño occurring during the summer can impact hurricane season. El Niño during the summer and fall can turn to weaker and a lower number of hurricanes in the Atlantic. This is because, the stronger El Niño means more shear in the Atlantic waters and hurricanes don’t like shear.If this forecast holds in the winter, seeing a continued El Niño trend, it could bring the jet streams northward. Therefore, a cooler and wetter trend could be in store for the South. The North then typically shows warmer and drier conditions. Feel more informed, prepared, and connected with FOX Carolina.
